options: A living thing that eats other living things
A living thing that makes its own food
questions.explanation: A consumer cannot make its own food, so it must eat other living things to get energy.
questions.misconception: Consumers eat for energy; producers make their own food instead.

questions.explanation: Herbivores like rabbits, deer, and cows eat only plants.
questions.misconception: Herbivore means plant-eater; animal-eaters are carnivores.

questions.explanation: A lion hunts and eats other animals, making it a carnivore.
questions.misconception: Carnivores eat meat; plant-eaters are herbivores.

questions.prompt: Where does a consumer's energy come from in the end?
questions.explanation: Plants capture the sun's energy first, and every consumer gets that energy by eating plants (or animals that ate plants).
questions.misconception: Even meat-eaters depend on plants, because their prey ate plants.
